author: Copilot
body:
When include_count is false, total_items is set to -1 as a sentinel, but total_pages is still computed later using that value. This yields misleading pagination metadata (e.g., total_pages becomes 0 for most limits). Consider setting total_pages=None (or another sentinel) whenever include_count is false, and guard the total_pages calculation to only run when total_items >= 0.
```suggestion
            # When include_count is False, leave total_items as None to indicate that
            # the total number of items is unknown and avoid misleading pagination metadata.
```

author: Copilot
body:
The JSON export path is documented/handled as NDJSON (one JSON object per line), but the zero-row case writes "[]" (a JSON array). This makes the file format inconsistent between empty vs non-empty exports and can break line-based NDJSON consumers. Prefer returning an empty string (or a trailing newline) for empty NDJSON exports, or switch all JSON exports to a single JSON array consistently.
```suggestion
                    content = ""
```

author: Copilot
body: _EXPORT_MAX_SIZE_BYTES is expressed in bytes, but the truncation check uses StringIO.tell(), which counts characters (not UTF-8 bytes). With non-ASCII content, the actual byte size can exceed the intended ~100MB cap, undermining the OOM protection. Consider tracking size in bytes (e.g., encode each written chunk and count bytes, or use BytesIO and write UTF-8 bytes).

author: Copilot
body: get_notification_export_file uses AsyncClient.get(), which eagerly reads the full response body; iter_bytes() will then iterate over an in-memory buffer rather than truly streaming. For large exports (even capped at ~100MB), this can cause unnecessary memory pressure in the BFF. Consider switching to httpx streaming (client.stream('GET', ...) / Response.aiter_bytes()) so the file is proxied chunk-by-chunk.

author: Copilot
body:
NotificationRecordExportParamsSchema currently allows dateRange values (P7D/P14D/P30D) that the BFF export endpoint rejects (it only allows up to P1D). This weakens client-side contract validation and can lead to requests that pass Zod parsing but fail at runtime. Consider splitting filter date-range vs export date-range schemas, or restricting this export params enum to the exportable presets only and handling the longer ranges exclusively in the UI filter schema.
```suggestion
    dateRange: z.enum(['PT15M', 'PT1H', 'PT6H', 'P1D']).optional(),
```

author: Copilot
body: The export truncation cap is enforced using UTF-8 byte counts, but the content is still accumulated in an io.StringIO (Python str). If any non-ASCII characters appear (e.g., in message/appliance_name), the in-memory representation can be 2–4 bytes/char, so peak memory usage can significantly exceed the intended ~100MB cap. To make the OOM protection reliable, consider switching to an io.BytesIO (write UTF-8 bytes) or streaming directly to S3 in chunks/multipart rather than building a large in-memory string.

author: Copilot
body:
`NotificationExportHandler` is intended to handle errors via toasts, but `useQuery` will still *throw* `HTTPPermissionError` by default (see `useQuery` wrapper), which can bubble to an error boundary and take down the authed layout when `/notifications/exports/:id` returns 403 (e.g., permission change/session state). Pass `throwPermissionError: false` and handle permission errors in the existing toast/cleanup flow (similar to `NotificationsPage`/`NotificationBell`).
```suggestion
    throwOnError: false,
    throwPermissionError: false,
```

author: Copilot
body: `downloadingRef` is a single global guard, but `exportId` is cleared before `downloadNotificationRecords()` finishes. This allows the user to start a second export while the first download is still in progress; if the second export reaches `completed` during that time, the handler will skip it (because `downloadingRef.current` is true) and it may never re-trigger once the first download completes (refs don’t cause rerenders). Consider either keeping `exportId` set until the download promise settles (so the button remains disabled), or tracking download-in-progress/queued export IDs in state so completed exports aren’t dropped.

author: Copilot
body:
Exports don’t use pagination totals, but `get_notifications()` defaults `include_count=True`, which triggers an extra COUNT(*) query. Since this path can read many pages, it’s worth explicitly setting `include_count=False` for export queries to reduce DB load and latency.
```suggestion
            kwargs["limit"] = 1000
            # Exports don't need pagination totals; avoid extra COUNT(*) queries by default.
            kwargs.setdefault("include_count", False)
```

author: Copilot
body:
The size cap check happens after writing the line to the buffer, so the export can exceed the intended ~100MB limit by up to the size of the last row (which may be large if fields like `arguments` are sizable). To enforce the cap more reliably, compute the UTF-8 byte size of the next line and stop before writing when it would cross the limit.
```suggestion
                line_bytes = len(line.encode("utf-8"))
                if byte_count + line_bytes > _EXPORT_MAX_SIZE_BYTES:
                    truncated = True
                    break
                buffer.write(line)
                byte_count += line_bytes
```

author: Copilot
body:
`get_notification_export_file` is being called without `await` inside an async function, which will typically pass a coroutine object into `StreamingResponse` (breaking streaming at runtime). Revert to awaiting the client call (or, if the client method was intentionally changed to return an async byte iterator, rename/adjust the client API so it is not an async function returning a coroutine).
```suggestion
        stream = await self.portal_api_client.get_notification_export_file(file_id=export_id)
```

author: Copilot
body:
Defaulting `include_count` to `True` can introduce an unconditional COUNT query (or equivalent) for every notifications request from any direct WebAPI consumer, which is a potential performance regression. Consider defaulting this to `False` and having the clients explicitly opt-in when they need counts (or document why `True` is safe/cheap in your implementation).
```suggestion
    include_count: bool = False
```

This script logs secrets (`service_key_secret`) to the Postman console, which can leak credentials via shared logs/screenshots/CI artifacts. Keep setting the environment variable if needed, but remove secret logging (or redact it) and consider storing secrets only in local (non-synced) environments.

